data_description.connection_mode: How Home Assistant reaches the thermostats. The local modes are experimental and need a DNS record on your network; read the documentation before you choose one.

gateway.title: Local connection
gateway.description:
In a local mode the thermostats connect to Home Assistant instead of OJ's gateway.

1. On the DNS server your thermostats use, add a record that points `{hostname}` to `{ip}`.
2. Make sure the thermostats can reach port {port} on that address.
3. Submit this form, then restart each thermostat so it looks up the address again.

With the relay, Home Assistant passes the connection on to OJ's gateway and the app keeps working. Local only works after a thermostat has connected through the relay once.

error.dns_not_detected: Home Assistant does not see the DNS record yet. Your thermostats may use another DNS server than Home Assistant does. Submit again to continue anyway.
error.dns_still_local: The DNS record still points the thermostats at Home Assistant, so they cannot reach the cloud. Remove the record and restart the thermostats. Submit again to continue anyway.
error.no_profile: Local only needs a thermostat that has connected through the relay once. Choose local with relay first, and switch after a thermostat has connected.

set_vacation.name: Set vacation
set_vacation.description: Schedule a vacation for the thermostat's group (WD5 series). The vacation runs from 00:00 on the start date until 00:00 on the end date; if it has already started, vacation mode is activated immediately.

start_date.name: Start date
start_date.description: The first day of the vacation.

cancel_vacation.name: Cancel vacation
cancel_vacation.description: Cancel the scheduled or active vacation for the thermostat's group (WD5 series). An active vacation returns to schedule or manual mode, whichever was used last.

set_schedule.name: Set schedule
set_schedule.description: Set the events of one or more weekdays in the thermostat group's weekly schedule (WD5 series). Up to 6 events per day, on the quarter hour, at least 15 minutes apart; a time earlier than the previous one is after midnight (03:00 at the latest).

events.name: Events
events.description: The day's events in order, each with a time (HH:MM) and a temperature (5-40 °C).

gateway_no_thermostat.title: No thermostat has connected to Home Assistant
gateway_no_thermostat.description: The connection is set to local, but no thermostat has connected to Home Assistant yet. Check that `{hostname}` points to `{ip}` on the DNS server your thermostats use, and that they can reach port {port} on that address. Then restart the thermostat so it looks up the address again. This message disappears when a thermostat connects.

gateway_untrusted.title: OJ's gateway shows an unexpected certificate
gateway_untrusted.description: The certificate of `{hostname}` is not the one this integration expects, so nothing is passed on to it. Thermostats that connected before are answered by Home Assistant, and the app shows them offline. OJ may have replaced its certificate, which needs an update of this integration. Please report it.
